definition_lines: Syntactic parallelism refers to the repetition of a word at the beginning of 2 or more consecutive sentences.
templates: Syntactically parallelising the repeated opening '[word]' in '[sentence 1]' and '[sentence 2]', (author) repetitiously underscores ..., positioning ...
examples: Syntactically parallelising the repeated opening ‘we’ in ‘We report the incident. We support the worker’ and ‘We must protect the community’, Wargan repetitiously underscores the collective responsibility of Roxburgh Park residents, creating rhythmic insistence that mobilise them to view safe intervention as a shared duty.
